page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the n4 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a performance profile characterized by average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1564.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core execution is limited, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 3219.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds at 33.17 GB/sec and 21.19 GB/sec respectively.

Despite weak multi-core performance and database operation metrics, the instance maintains average performance in specific tasks such as static web serving at 7.0 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression. It also supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512. The high memory density relative to the vCPU count makes this instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel CPU processing, such as caching layers, lightweight in-memory databases, and moderate web serving.

Powered by an Intel processor with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading, it includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance does not feature local storage or integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0, but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth results. It achieves average throughput in static web serving at 7.0 GB/sec and single-threaded compression tasks. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and moderate single-thread performance, the n4-highmem-4 is best suited for memory-intensive workloads with low parallel computing demands, such as caching layers, small-scale databases, and general web serving.
